headline.headline: FRELICK, PRATT FUEL BREWERS' MIRACLE COMEBACK IN GAME 2
headline.deck: Milwaukee erases 4-0 first-inning deficit to stun Tampa Bay, seize commanding 2-0 Series lead
headline.body:
MILWAUKEE — Sal Frelick had not hit a home run in three months. Saturday night at American Family Field, he picked the perfect moment to end the drought. Frelick's shot tied the score and Cooper Pratt followed with a go-ahead single in the seventh inning as the Milwaukee Brewers completed a stunning 5-4 comeback victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 2 of the World Series, sending 43,245 delirious fans home with a two-games-to-none stranglehold on the Fall Classic.

The Rays appeared to have the evening well in hand after jumping on Brewers pitching for four runs in the very first inning, building a 4-0 lead that looked insurmountable against a Tampa Bay staff riding high on momentum. Milwaukee answered with a single run in the fourth, another in the sixth, and the tying blow from Frelick before Pratt's clutch single in the seventh put the Brewers ahead 5-4 for good. The Rays went scoreless over the final eight frames, unable to recapture the electricity of that explosive opening.

The box score tells the story of Milwaukee's resilience inning by inning: zeros across innings two through nine for Tampa Bay, while the Brewers chipped away with single runs in the fourth, sixth, and seventh before holding firm the rest of the way. The Rays' Jordan Hicks was hit by a pitch from D. Hall and was lifted for a pinch hitter in the eighth. Game 3 shifts to Tampa Bay as a Brewers club that once looked dead in the first inning now controls its own destiny in the chase for a championship.

secondary.headline: HORNETS STING HEAT 115-110 TO KEEP SECOND-ROUND PUSH ALIVE
secondary.deck: Charlotte survives Miami in a five-point thriller to advance its conference semifinal run
secondary.body:
CHARLOTTE — The Charlotte Hornets refused to wilt under the heat of a playoff atmosphere Saturday, outlasting the Miami Heat 115-110 in a hard-fought conference semifinal contest that came down to the final possessions. The five-point final margin understated how closely contested the game was throughout, with Miami pressing Charlotte at every turn inside Spectrum Center.

Elsewhere in the Eastern Conference semifinals, the Cleveland Cavaliers edged the Brooklyn Nets 125-121 in a tightly contested affair that required the Cavaliers to hold off a late Nets charge. The Philadelphia 76ers, already covered extensively on the sport pages, continued their dominant run. The Hornets' win stands as the evening's tightest finish among the three NBA playoff games, keeping Charlotte firmly in the hunt as the second round intensifies.

secondary.headline: KAPRIZOV STRIKES 26 SECONDS IN AS WILD ROLL PAST KRAKEN 5-1
secondary.deck: Minnesota's superstar sets the tone immediately as Wild cruise to a lopsided second-round victory
secondary.body:
MINNEAPOLIS — Kirill Kaprizov did not wait long to announce his intentions. The Minnesota Wild winger put the puck past Seattle goaltending just 26 seconds into Saturday's second-round playoff game, setting a tone that never wavered as the Wild rolled to a dominant 5-1 victory over the Kraken. Minnesota controlled the contest from the opening moments, building a lead the Kraken could never seriously threaten.

The win gave Minnesota a commanding presence in the second round as the Wild demonstrated why they are among the conference's most dangerous teams. Meanwhile, the Calgary Flames also continued to surge, defeating the Detroit Red Wings 4-1 for their third consecutive victory with Joel Farabee recording a goal and two assists. The second round of the NHL playoffs is shaping up as a showcase for teams peaking at precisely the right time.

secondary.headline: LARRY FITZGERALD TO ENTER CARDINALS RING OF HONOR
secondary.deck: Arizona's all-time great receiver receives his franchise's highest distinction this weekend
secondary.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. — Larry Fitzgerald, the greatest wide receiver in Arizona Cardinals history and one of the most celebrated players of his NFL generation, is set to enter the Cardinals Ring of Honor this weekend, receiving the highest distinction his franchise can bestow. Fitzgerald, who spent his entire storied career in Arizona and retired as one of the game's all-time leading receivers, spoke publicly before the ceremony about what the honor means to him and to the organization he defined for two decades.

The induction caps an offseason in which NFL franchises across the league have turned their attention to legacy and roster reconstruction in equal measure. With Super Bowl LX now several months in the rearview mirror following the conclusion of the 2025 season last February, the league is in full rebuild mode heading toward 2026. Fitzgerald's Ring of Honor moment offers a welcome reminder of what sustained excellence and loyalty to one franchise can produce over the course of a career.

column.headline: THE BREWERS HAVE Tampa BAY RIGHT WHERE THEY WANT THEM
column.body:
No team in World Series history has ever come back from a two-games-to-none deficit to win the championship more than a handful of times, and the Rays now find themselves staring down that steep hill after surrendering a 4-0 lead Saturday night in Milwaukee. What makes the Brewers' position even more impressive is how they won it, not with a big inning or a blowout, but with grinding, methodical single runs in the fourth, sixth, and seventh that proved Tampa Bay could not protect its early advantage. That kind of comeback leaves a psychological mark that does not fade easily.

Sal Frelick had not homered in three months. Cooper Pratt's name was not on anyone's lips heading into October. Yet there they were, delivering the biggest hits of the season on the sport's grandest stage. That is the story of this Brewers team, and it is why Tampa Bay should be genuinely worried heading home for Game 3. Milwaukee does not need stars to beat you. It just needs enough players willing to step up at the right moment, and right now it has plenty of them.

story.headline: BREWERS ERASE 4-RUN HOLE TO SEIZE 2-0 WORLD SERIES STRANGLEHOLD ON RAYS
story.deck: Milwaukee rallies from first-inning disaster, wins 5-4 to push Tampa Bay to the brink
story.body:
MILWAUKEE, Oct. 24 -- The Tampa Bay Rays scored four runs in the first inning Saturday night and appeared to have American Family Field right where they wanted it. They did not count on the Milwaukee Brewers. Fueled by home runs from Aaron Frelick and Aaron Hicks and a relentless parade of stolen bases, Milwaukee clawed back run by run across the middle innings to win Game 2 of the World Series, 5-4, before 43,245 fans, taking a commanding 2-0 series lead and pushing the Rays to the edge of elimination.

The Brewers answered the first-inning four-spot with two runs of their own in that frame, then chipped away with single tallies in the fourth, sixth, and seventh innings to complete the comeback. Frelick's home run provided the decisive blow, while contributions from Christian Yelich, William Contreras, and Joey Wiemer, who swiped bases along with Jackson Chourio, Sal Frelick, and others, kept Milwaukee's offense churning. The Rays stranded 14 baserunners and could not manufacture a single run after the opening frame, a failure of execution that now looms enormous with the series shifting back to St. Petersburg.

Jonathan Aranda and Taylor Walls each reached base repeatedly for Tampa Bay, with Aranda doubling among the Rays' scattered hits, but Hall D. was touched for the early damage and Milwaukee's pitching staff slammed the door for eight straight scoreless innings. The game lasted 3 hours and 38 minutes. Milwaukee, which has now erased multiple-run deficits repeatedly this October, looks every bit the inevitable champion its October resume suggests.

story.headline: 76ERS STAY PERFECT, POUND BUCKS 127-116 TO OPEN THREE-GAME HOMESTAND
story.deck: Philadelphia rolls to 3-0 start, now faces unbeaten Detroit in marquee Eastern matchup Sunday.
story.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The Philadelphia 76ers are three games into the 2026-27 season and still looking for a team that can stop them. Philadelphia dispatched the Milwaukee Bucks 127-116 at home Friday night, pushing the Sixers to 3-0 and cementing their place atop the Eastern Conference standings heading into what promises to be the young season's first genuine test.

The victory sets up a collision Sunday between the NBA's only two undefeated teams in the East. The Detroit Pistons arrive at 2-0 and sitting second in the conference, meaning someone's perfect record falls when the opening tip goes up. Philadelphia has won three straight while Milwaukee drops to a precarious position early in the year, the 11-point margin suggesting the Sixers controlled the game's important stretches.

Elsewhere Friday, the Cleveland Cavaliers edged the Brooklyn Nets 125-121 in a tight contest at Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse, the four-point final obscuring what appeared to be a competitive night throughout. Charlotte also turned back Miami 115-110, dropping the Heat to 0-3 and deepening a miserable start to their season. Miami faces Dallas on Sunday in a matchup of struggling clubs, with the Heat desperate to avoid falling four games below the break-even line before October ends.

story.headline: DRAISAITL POWERS OILERS PAST RED WINGS AS EDMONTON ROLLS TO 8-2-1
story.deck: Leon Draisaitl nets two goals as Edmonton thumps Detroit to stay atop the Pacific.
story.body:
Leon Draisaitl was at it again Friday night, potting two goals to lead the Edmonton Oilers past the Detroit Red Wings in a game that reinforced just how dominant the Pacific Division leaders have been through the early weeks of the 2026-27 season. The Oilers, now 8-2-1, have established themselves as one of the NHL's elite clubs, and Draisaitl's latest multi-goal performance only added to his reputation as the most dangerous scoring threat in the Western Conference.

Elsewhere around the league Saturday, William Nylander carried his two-goal momentum into the week as the Toronto Maple Leafs, sitting at 7-4-2 in the Atlantic Division, traveled to Calgary to face a Flames club that has stumbled to a 4-6 record. In Vancouver, the Minnesota Wild brought a 7-3-2 mark and the hot stick of Blake Coleman, who tallied twice in his last outing, into Rogers Arena to face a Canucks team that has been one of the league's most disappointing outfits at 2-9-1.

The New York Rangers look to extend their home winning streak Sunday when they welcome the Los Angeles Kings, who are 2-5-2 and searching for consistency on the road. Nashville, meanwhile, hosts the Colorado Avalanche in a Central Division clash that carries real weight, with the Avalanche at 6-4-1 pressing against the Predators, who sit at an even 3-3-4 and need a statement win to separate themselves from the bottom of the division standings.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026 SEASON
story.deck: Several franchises are reshaping their rosters around new signal-callers this spring.
story.body:
The NFL's offseason quarterback market exploded this May with a flurry of moves that have reshuffled the power structure across both conferences. The Las Vegas Raiders made the boldest splash, agreeing to a four-year, $176 million contract with veteran quarterback Sam Darnold, who parlayed a strong 2025 campaign into the richest deal of his career. Meanwhile, the Cleveland Browns sent shockwaves through the league by trading three draft picks to the Pittsburgh Steelers in exchange for Russell Wilson, reuniting the 37-year-old gunslinger with offensive coordinator Ken Dorsey in what both sides are calling a win-now gamble.

The 2026 NFL Draft, held in Indianapolis last month, further stirred the pot at the position. Colorado's Shedeur Sanders, widely projected as the top overall pick, slid unexpectedly to the Tennessee Titans at No. 4 after the New York Giants and Cleveland Browns traded away their picks. The Titans immediately signed Sanders to his rookie deal and released veteran Ryan Tannehill, closing a significant chapter in Nashville's football history. Draft analysts have praised the haul assembled by general managers who traded down, with the New England Patriots collecting three second-round selections in a single evening.

Training camps remain months away, but minicamps opening across the league this week are already generating headline-worthy moments. Wide receiver Davante Adams, who signed with the Dallas Cowboys in March, drew loud cheers during organized team activities at The Star in Frisco when he hauled in a contested touchdown grab over cornerback DaRon Bland. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones called the 33-year-old Adams the missing piece for a squad that fell one game short of Super Bowl LX in February. For a league that never truly sleeps, May 2026 is proving to be one of its more restless offseasons in recent memory.
